newsitem.title: USA: U.S. debt futures end pit trade higher, off peaks.
newsitem.headline: U.S. debt futures end pit trade higher, off peaks.

text.p: U.S. debt futures ended higher, but most units closed just below day's price peaks.
Traders said action wound down during the afternoon, after the market showed little response to the Treasury's announcement of its quarterly refunding package.
Treasury next week will sell $38.0 billion of securities, comprised of $10.0 billion in 30-year bonds, $12.0 billion of 10-year notes and $16.0 billion in three-year notes.
Floor brokers said the news had no effect, although consensus estimates had pegged the total refunding package at $40.0 billion, including $14.0 billion in 10-year notes.
"There was absolutely zero reaction," said one floor broker of bond futures.

Instead, September T-bond futures rose to 116-19/32 after midday, hitting its highest price since early February 1996, partly on technical buying and ideas that U.S. economic fundamentals thus far show few solid signs of inflation to cause the Federal Reserve to tighten credit.
Traders still waited for Friday's July U.S. employment report and said the market could prove vulnerable to long profittaking, given its lofty price levels.
But they also said few were willing to step in and sell the contract without strong provocation.
"We are getting a little expensive up here, a little overbought, but no one, no one, is willing to sell it," said the first floor broker.
He pegged the next resistance for September T-bonds at the 116-23/32 to 28/32 area, with another objective at about 117-10/32-12/32, roughly 6.25-percent cash equivalent yield.
Brokers reported all-around buying Wednesday, including from dealers, banks, and funds. They also saw more mortgage- backed-related buying in the long- and intermediate- sectors.

September T-bonds ended up 14/32 at 116-12/32, 10-year notes rose 8/32 to 110-24/32, munis gained 16/32 to 122-02/32, Dec T-bills added 0.030 to 94.875, and Eurodollars gained 0.030 to 94.185. -Derivatives desk (312)408-8750/E-Mail:derivatives@reuters.com
